blocks.title: Stats worksheets catch-up, then start the proposal
blocks.note:
1. Check which worksheets show as missing on Canvas (2 min)
2. Email the stats team about any practicals you missed (10 min)
3. Do the matching R tutorial (25 min)
4. Proposal: open the brief and read only the first part (3 min)
5. Proposal: open the Developing your Research Proposal worksheet (3 min)

blocks.title: Stats mop-up quiz, then proposal ideas
blocks.note:
Rent is due today, pay it first (5 min).
1. Stats mop-up quiz (20 min)
2. Proposal: redo the attention experiment demo (10 min)
3. Proposal: read Forster & Lavie (2009), abstract and figures only (15 min)
4. Proposal: jot 3 ideas for a repeated-measures variable (15 min)

blocks.title: Cognitive Psychology proposal: pick your idea
blocks.note:
1. Fill in the worksheet: idea, hypotheses, conditions (20 min)
2. Find 2 more papers that back up your idea (25 min)
Spare time: start the Introduction.

blocks.title: Cognitive Psychology proposal: write the Introduction
blocks.note:
1. Write the Introduction, ending with your hypotheses (25 min, take longer if it's flowing)
2. Dev Psych: read the three essay questions and pick one (5 min)
3. Dev Psych: open the matching seminar page and note its two essential readings (5 min)

blocks.title: Proposal Method, then a first look at the poster
blocks.note:
Payday today.
1. Proposal: write the Method in future tense (25 min)
2. Neuro poster: find which question you were given (5 min)
3. Neuro poster: download the template and save a copy (3 min)
4. Neuro poster: look through the annotated example (10 min)
